title: 9.11.2: Practice Test
originalText:
Practice Test

Is the following ordered pair a solution to the system of equations?

1.

\(\begin{matrix}\\\begin{matrix}−5x−y=12\\x+4y=9\end{matrix}\end{matrix}\) with \((−3,3)\)

For the following exercises, solve the systems of linear and nonlinear equations using substitution or elimination. Indicate if no solution exists.

2.

\(\begin{matrix}\frac{1}{2}x−\frac{1}{3}y=4\\\frac{3}{2}x−y=0\end{matrix}\)

3.

\(\begin{matrix}\\−\frac{1}{2}x−4y=4\\2x+16y=2\end{matrix}\)

4.

\(\begin{matrix}5x−y=1\\−10x+2y=−2\end{matrix}\)

5.

\(\begin{matrix}4x−6y−2z=\frac{1}{10}\\x−7y+5z=−\frac{1}{4}\\3x+6y−9z=\frac{6}{5}\end{matrix}\)

6.

\(\begin{matrix}x+z=20\\x+y+z=20\\x+2y+z=10\end{matrix}\)

7.

\(\begin{matrix}5x−4y−3z=0\\2x+y+2z=0\\x−6y−7z=0\end{matrix}\)

8.

\(\begin{matrix}y={x}^{2}+2x−3\\y=x−1\end{matrix}\)

9.

\(\begin{matrix}{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}=25\\{y}^{2}−2{x}^{2}=1\end{matrix}\)

For the following exercises, graph the following inequalities.

10.

\(y<{x}^{2}+9\)

11.

\(\begin{matrix}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}>4\\y<{x}^{2}+1\end{matrix}\)

For the following exercises, write the partial fraction decomposition.

12.

\(\frac{−8x−30}{{x}^{2}+10x+25}\)

13.

\(\frac{13x+2}{{(3x+1)}^{2}}\)

14.

\(\frac{{x}^{4}−{x}^{3}+2x−1}{x{({x}^{2}+1)}^{2}}\)

For the following exercises, perform the given matrix operations.

15.

\(5[\begin{matrix}4&9\\−2&3\end{matrix}]+\frac{1}{2}[\begin{matrix}−6&12\\4&−8\end{matrix}]\)

16.

\([\begin{matrix}1&4&−7\\−2&9&5\\12&0&−4\end{matrix}] [\begin{matrix}3&−4\\1&3\\5&10\end{matrix}]\)

17.

\({[\begin{matrix}\frac{1}{2}&\frac{1}{3}\\\frac{1}{4}&\frac{1}{5}\end{matrix}]}^{−1}\)

18.

\(det|\begin{matrix}0&0\\400&4,000\end{matrix}|\)

19.

\(det|\begin{matrix}\frac{1}{2}&−\frac{1}{2}&0\\−\frac{1}{2}&0&\frac{1}{2}\\0&\frac{1}{2}&0\end{matrix}|\)

20.

If \(det(A)=−6,\) what would be the determinant if you switched rows 1 and 3, multiplied the second row by 12, and took the inverse?

21.

Rewrite the system of linear equations as an augmented matrix.

\(\begin{matrix}14x−2y+13z=140\\−2x+3y−6z=−1\\x−5y+12z=11\end{matrix}\)

22.

Rewrite the augmented matrix as a system of linear equations.

\([\begin{matrix}1&0&3\\−2&4&9\\−6&1&2\end{matrix}|\begin{matrix}12\\−5\\8\end{matrix}]\)

For the following exercises, use Gaussian elimination to solve the systems of equations.

23.

\(\begin{matrix}x−6y=4\\2x−12y=0\end{matrix}\)

24.

\(\begin{matrix}2x+y+z=−3\\x−2y+3z=6\\x−y−z=6\end{matrix}\)

For the following exercises, use the inverse of a matrix to solve the systems of equations.

25.

\(\begin{matrix}4x−5y=−50\\−x+2y=80\end{matrix}\)

26.

\(\begin{matrix}\frac{1}{100}x−\frac{3}{100}y+\frac{1}{20}z=−49\\\frac{3}{100}x−\frac{7}{100}y−\frac{1}{100}z=13\\\frac{9}{100}x−\frac{9}{100}y−\frac{9}{100}z=99\end{matrix}\)

For the following exercises, use Cramer’s Rule to solve the systems of equations.

27.

\(\begin{matrix}200x−300y=2\\400x+715y=4\end{matrix}\)

28.

\(\begin{matrix}0.1x+0.1y−0.1z=−1.2\\0.1x−0.2y+0.4z=−1.2\\0.5x−0.3y+0.8z=−5.9\end{matrix}\)

For the following exercises, solve using a system of linear equations.

29.

A factory producing cell phones has the following cost and revenue functions: \(C(x)={x}^{2}+75x+2,688\) and \(R(x)={x}^{2}+160x.\) What is the range of cell phones they should produce each day so there is profit? Round to the nearest number that generates profit.

30.

A small fair charges $1.50 for students, $1 for children, and $2 for adults. In one day, three times as many children as adults attended. A total of 800 tickets were sold for a total revenue of $1,050. How many of each type of ticket was sold?
